items.stem: What is meant by a switch?
items.answer: A device used to open or close an electric circuit

items.stem: A bulb does not glow when the switch is OFF because:
items.answer: the circuit is open
items.markingKey: (b) the circuit is open.

items.stem:

items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.

options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a good conductor of electricity?
items.answer: dry wood
items.markingKey: (d) Dry wood is an insulator, not a good conductor of electricity. Each of the others (aluminium foil, silver spoon, steel key) is a good conductor of electricity.

items.stem: Aditi made a conduction tester with a cell, a bulb and two free wire ends, and touched the free ends to each of these in turn: rubber band, steel key, plastic scale, silver spoon. For which objects will the bulb glow? Give a reason.
items.answer: Bulb glows for silver spoon, steel key; not for plastic scale, rubber band.

items.stem: Diya says that since tap water conducts electricity, sea water must conduct even better. Is she right? Explain how you could test it.
items.answer: Yes, sea water has more dissolved salts so it conducts better. Test with a tester (cell, LED and wires): the LED glows brighter in salt water than in tap water.

items.stem:
Read: In winter, Manish's family in Shimla plugged a room heater, an electric kettle and an iron into a single multi-plug socket. After a few minutes, the MCB tripped and the lights went off.
(i) Why did the MCB trip? (ii) What could have happened without the MCB? (iii) Which effect of current do all three appliances use? (iv) Give one safe practice.
items.answer: (i) Overloading drew too much current. (ii) Wires could overheat and cause a fire. (iii) Heating effect. (iv) Do not run many high-power appliances from one socket; use separate sockets.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each.

items.stem: Suggest why the electrical wiring of old houses sometimes catches fire when many new appliances are added.
items.answer: The old wires were not designed for large currents; overloading heats them, the insulation melts and a short circuit or fire can occur, especially if fuses were replaced with thick wire.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: overloading. 1 mark: overheating and melted insulation.

items.stem: Describe how you would safely help a person who is stuck to a live wire after getting an electric shock.
items.answer: Do not touch the person; switch off the main supply or pull out the plug; if not possible, push the wire away using a dry wooden stick or plastic; then call for medical help.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: do not touch. 1 mark: cut supply/insulator. 1 mark: medical help.

items.stem: Ananya's electric bell only buzzes once and then stays silent while she keeps the switch pressed. Suggest a fault and explain.
items.answer: The contact screw is not touching the iron strip again (badly adjusted or dirty), so after the first attraction the circuit stays broken and the hammer cannot repeat.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: contact screw fault. 1 mark: circuit stays open.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT an insulator?
items.answer: graphite (pencil lead)
items.markingKey: (d) Graphite (pencil lead) is a good conductor of electricity, not an insulator. Each of the others (plastic scale, paper, dry wood) is an insulator.
